title: Stop the violence! and go see Brittany S Pierce live Off-Broadway!!  ...
transcript: Heather Morris, aka Brittany on Glee, just made her off Broadway debut last night in 11 to midnight. And obviously, I had to be there, so let's talk about it. So if you don't know, 11 to midnight is a brand new off Broadway show from the minds of Cost n Mayor. Cost n mayor absolutely blew up on TikTok, doing little mini choreographed dances to phone ringtones and commercial jingles. But they've never done anything at this scale. Like this is a full 65 minute show with characters and a storyline. And while there is some dialogue, it is mostly told through the medium of dance, which is what makes this the perfect show for Heather Morris to join, because in addition to initially being hired as a dancer on Glee, she actually got her start as a backup dancer for Beyonce. And she really gets to show the full breadth of her dance moves in the show. In addition to a few moments of comedy that you've come to expect from her in roles like Britney S Pierce on Glee. One thing I was not expecting is just how much audience participation is in the show. If you are in the front row or on the first couple of aisles, definitely be prepared for a cast member to come up to you and ask you to be a part of the show. One of the more involved moments of audience participation involved teaching an audience member some dance moves Before the show and then during the show, inviting them up on stage to do them in front of everyone. Mine was thankfully a lot less involved. I was given a map that I had to give to the character played by Melissa B. Craft. This is part of a fantasy sequence where she is going on a quest to fight a dragon played by Heather Morris. And as a big fantasy nerd, it might have been my favourite moment in the show. Heather as a dragon has this big, flowing, defying gravity Elphaba cape, and it's so simple, it's just some fans and a cloth, and yet it feels so epic. And that kind of ingenuity is all throughout the show. They're constantly using everyday items like phone flashlights or post it notes to create some really cool imagery. And while I don't think this show is saying or doing anything particularly groundbreaking, it is just a really fun time. And at only 65 minutes, it flies by. And so if you are a fan of dance or movement pieces or just a fan of Heather's work on Glee, I definitely think this is one to check out.
reasoning: The reviewer clearly recommends the show with enthusiasm, highlighting Heather Morris's performance, creative staging, and overall fun factor, while acknowledging it's not groundbreaking. The positive language and direct recommendation signal a solid positive review.
